requirements.title: College of Science core
requirements.summary: Complete the linked college areas, with the reviewed overlap, approval and experiential policies below. Some university and approved-course-list details remain unresolved; do not sum overlapping areas.

requirements.title: Approved writing courses
requirements.summary: Source course pool. Combined courses satisfy both components; separate writing and presentation choices or approved experience are alternatives. University oral communication approvals also satisfy presentation.

requirements.title: Approved presentation courses
requirements.summary: Source course pool. Combined courses satisfy both components; separate writing and presentation choices or approved experience are alternatives. University oral communication approvals also satisfy presentation.

requirements.title: Approved combined courses
requirements.summary: Source course pool. Combined courses satisfy both components; separate writing and presentation choices or approved experience are alternatives. University oral communication approvals also satisfy presentation.

requirements.title: Approved Great Issues titles
requirements.summary: Only the listed titles are approved, including variable-title courses. The Level column is a course level, not credits; listed semesters are not approval expiry dates.

requirements.title: Written Communication
requirements.summary: Complete an approved University Core Written Communication course. The historical SAT/ACT waiver applies only to Fall 2011–2013 admission terms, not the current cohort.

requirements.title: Technical Writing and Technical Presentation
requirements.summary: Meet both writing and presentation through an approved combined course, an approved course for each component, or approved experiential work. This also meets University Core Oral Communication. COM 11400 elective credit and COM 21700 may both count toward the degree.

requirements.title: Technical-writing experience alternatives
requirements.summary: Approved experiential contract: lead/majority-authored peer-reviewed publication; a paper judged publishable by a Science faculty expert; or three approved papers of at least 1,500 words, including one persuasive argument. Students whose primary high-school instruction was not in English must use an approved writing course.

requirements.title: Technical-presentation experience alternatives
requirements.summary: Approved contract: sole/predominant scientific-meeting presentation, adjudicated poster with written judge feedback, internship/co-op presentation, or three approved science-course presentations of at least ten minutes each.

requirements.title: Teaming and Collaboration
requirements.summary: A listed teamwork course or approved experience meets this area. CS 18000 is explicitly approved from Fall 2011 onward, so the major requirement can meet it. Transfer/AP/IB/A-level credit cannot satisfy this experience.

requirements.title: Other approved teaming routes
requirements.summary: Other listed courses include BIOL 32800, CS 17700/30700/40800, EAPS 32700/36000/36400, EDCI 49800, ENGR 13000/13100/13200/13300/14100/16100, PHYS 17200, STAT 47201 and TECH 39900. ENTR courses exclude 46000 and need approval for variable titles; ENTR capstones, EPICS 10000–40000 and EPICS 49000, and ROTC are listed. TDM 10100+10200 also needs two semesters of Corporate Partnerships; alternatively choose three one-credit labs from MA 16290/26190/34990/41690. Approved co-op, internship or undergraduate research is permitted. Archived courses are excluded.

requirements.title: Experiential core approval and timing
requirements.summary: For teaming, language/culture, writing or presentation, the experience must occur during Purdue undergraduate study and have a scientific focus. Consult the advisor; submit contract and supervisor preapproval for faculty review, preferably before starting. Final supervisor documentation and student reflection/summary require faculty approval. Complete contracts one semester before anticipated graduation.

requirements.title: Language and Culture
requirements.summary: Choose one Fall 2023-and-forward route for this nine-credit area. Culture courses cannot also meet General Education or Great Issues, and one course cannot fill two components of an option. A noncredit waiver creates elective space; it does not reduce the minimum 120-hour degree.

requirements.title: Language and culture option 1
requirements.summary: Complete an approved two-course foreign-language sequence and one approved culture course.

requirements.title: Language and culture option 2
requirements.summary: Complete one approved language course, one approved culture course and approved short-term study abroad: at least eight days, a course of at least three credits, and significant local cultural immersion.

requirements.title: Language and culture option 3
requirements.summary: Complete three approved culture courses that build understanding of a culture or related aspects across cultures. At most one may be at the 10000 level; use 20000–40000 courses for the balance. Selections may span subjects but must build knowledge.

requirements.title: Language and culture option 4
requirements.summary: Complete approved study abroad plus one approved culture course. A noncredit waiver releases six credits for electives while retaining the 120-hour degree minimum.

requirements.title: Language and culture option 5
requirements.summary: International students may use their Purdue international experience for a partial waiver plus one approved culture course. Domestic students with additional cultural experience may seek advisor recommendation, interview and approval for the same partial waiver. Six credits become electives; the degree minimum remains 120. Full waivers described for pre-Fall-2023 catalogs do not apply to the current cohort.

requirements.title: General Education
requirements.summary: Complete three approved courses totaling nine credits. Across ACCT, AGEC, DSB, IBE, REAL, ECON, ENTR, FIN, MIS, MKTG, OBHR, QM, STRT and SCOM, at most one course/three credits may count. Courses cannot also meet language/culture or Great Issues. For variable numbers only approved titles count; listing is not an offering guarantee.

requirements.title: General education exclusions
requirements.summary: No independent research, Science-crosslisted course or laboratory/studio course. Excluded: PHIL 15000/45000/55000; PSY 20100/20400/30600/50000/50100; SOC 38200; COM 11400; all ENTR except 20000/20100.

requirements.title: Great Issues
requirements.summary: Complete an approved Great Issues title. Cannot also meet culture/diversity or general education. AP/IB/A-level credit does not qualify; accredited transfer coursework may be submitted through the advisor for associate-dean review. Variable-title approvals are title-specific.

requirements.title: Science Technology and Society
requirements.summary: Complete an approved University Core STS course. Completing the Statewide General Transfer Core does not fulfill this outcome; an STS course is still required.

requirements.title: Mathematics
requirements.summary: Complete single-variable calculus I and II: MA 16100 (5) or 16500 (4), followed by MA 16200 (5) or 16600 (4). The two sequences may be mixed. The applied-calculus exception is only for Biology majors.

requirements.title: Statistics
requirements.summary: Complete the statistics course approved for the major. The college lists STAT 30100/35000/35500/50300/51100 as subject to major approval; this does not override the AI major’s probability/statistics alternatives.

requirements.title: Computing
requirements.summary: Complete computing approved within the major; CS 17600 and CS 18000 appear on the college list and in the AI core. Other college options are not substitutions for AI major requirements without major approval.

requirements.title: Laboratory Science
requirements.summary: Complete a two-course, one-year laboratory-science sequence outside the major, from sequences approved for the individual plan. In-person laboratories are encouraged, not stated as mandatory.

requirements.title: Biology sequences
requirements.summary: BIOL 11000/11100 is listed for life scientists who are not Biology majors; applicability to AI needs plan approval. BIOL 12100/13100/13500 is also listed.

requirements.title: Chemistry sequences
requirements.summary: CHM 12500/12600 is listed. Another route is (CHM 11510 and either 11520 or 11530) then (11610 and either 11620 or 11630). A printed alternative combines CHM 11500 with either 11520 or 11530 and 12901; its malformed grouping/title text needs advisor clarification. CHM 12901 alone is only sufficient for Biological Sciences majors, not AI.

requirements.title: Earth science sequence
requirements.summary: EAPS 11100 and EAPS 11200, subject to the student’s plan approval.

requirements.title: Physics sequence
requirements.summary: Eight credits: Physics I (four credits) from PHYS 22000/17200/23300, and Physics II (four credits) from PHYS 22100/27200/23400 or the combined PHYS 24100+25200. The latter is a lecture/lab pair, not two independent alternatives.

requirements.title: Degree components and credit application
requirements.summary: Complete major, Science core and free-elective requirements. Purdue courses, AP/IB/CLEP and transfer credit apply according to the specific major’s rules; confirm in the individual degree plan. Any Purdue course may serve as a free elective, subject to the college’s major-specific not-recommended list.

requirements.title: University AI working competency
requirements.summary: Incoming Fall 2026 students must complete approved AI-focused coursework as a university core graduation requirement. Approved courses span one to four hours; the specific AI major course that fulfills this competency is not verified, so no additional credits are inferred.

requirements.summary: Choose one; the two approved calculus sequences may be mixed.

requirements.summary: Choose one; the two approved calculus sequences may be mixed.
